title: The phone's network allow-list is a hand copy of the adapters' routes, query keys and headers
evidence: Owner ruling 2026-11-27 (R17), replaced later that day so the list can be shared with a future Android app: one shared route table, a plain data file in the repo, is the single source. The cloud adapters read their routes from it. At build time it is generated into a constant compiled into the iPhone app (and later the Android app the same way), so no platform hand-writes a list. The native app, never the over-the-air engine, enforces it, so a new route takes effect only with a new app build. A change to the table is a security-class change (adversary + Codex). A test fails when an adapter uses a route outside the table. Build it after PR 2099 lands, since that PR edits dropbox-rest.ts and drive-rest.ts. Root fix R17 (triage 2026-11-25). ios/HealthRoadmap/Engine/EngineHTTP.swift:29-43 (routes, headers, credentialParameters) vs dropbox-rest.ts:19-24, drive-rest.ts:50-51. Agree today; fails closed. Hand list in EngineFenceTests. Fable ruled 2026-11-11: generate the allow-list from the adapters, with I-2 (replaced by the 2026-11-27 ruling). Security fence. iPhone survey 2026-11-11 (main fcc4ed9b) L9
